items.title: Diagnose why episode 0 stops at 17 steps with success=0
items.acceptance: Per-step action log identifies which agent emits action=0 and why
items.notes: Root cause: At step=2 a single bed detection (conf=0.888) crosses sem_threshold and locks found_goal=True. Its 3D back-projection writes a wrong target into object_pcd (truth distance 6.6m). For the next 14 steps the ShortestPathFollower drives the agent toward that incorrect 3D point. At step=17 the follower decides the goal is reached and returns 0; because found_goal is True, the override 'if not found_goal and action==0' does NOT trigger, so action=0 propagates to env.step and is_stop_called=True ends the episode. Recommended fixes: (a) require N-frame multi-confirmation before setting found_goal; (b) reset found_goal/object_pcd if proximity to nearest_point disagrees with detection; (c) raise --sem_threshold for synthetic+smoke scenes. Awaiting user choice.

items.title: Make flames penetrate smoke in the RGB sensor
items.acceptance: SmokeRGBSensor preserves flame pixels and adds a soft glow halo under dense smoke; HSV flame detector still fires on the smoke-attenuated RGB.
items.notes: Added flame_* knobs to SmokeRGBConfig (passthrough/glow/color bleed/HSV ranges). Rewrote SmokeRGBSensor: HSV flame mask + Gaussian glow boost transmittance T'=T+(1-T)*boost; surrounding smoke gets tinted by the local fire color; particulate noise is suppressed on the flame core. Verified with scripts/test_rgb_flame_through_smoke.py (flame mean RGB=240,111,44 vs bg 179,179,178 at density=0.9, 4 m) and scripts/test_flame_after_smoke.py (HSV detector returns one box, score 0.950).

items.title: Voxel renderer: flame penetrates smoke; teleop dashboard layout fix
items.acceptance: Volumetric composite uses two transmittance accumulators so flame emission isn't eaten by smoke; teleop window shows RGB / Depth (smoke-degraded) / Thermal (INFERNO) instead of two depth-like panels.
items.notes: Added VoxelRenderParams.flame_smoke_passthrough (default 0.85). The marcher now keeps a separate T_acc_flame that uses (1-passthrough)*smoke_k + flame_k as the optical depth, so flame radiation leaks through smoke just like real visible-band fire imagery (Starr & Lattimer 2014 Fig. 7). Exposed via VoxelSmokeConfig + the legacy FireWorldRenderer shim. keyboard_teleop_fire.py now renders 3 panels (RGB / Depth-smoke / Thermal-INFERNO), forces thermal_color_blend=1.0 so it visually differs from JET-colored depth, always shows the suite's degraded depth (independent of --depth_use_clean), and exposes --flame-smoke-passthrough. Verified with a 1-ray micro test: with passthrough=0.0 a flame behind a smoke wall yields neutral grey RGB (R-B=0); with passthrough=0.85 the same configuration produces a warm tint (R=230, B=207). Existing scripts/test_fire_world_step_clock.py still passes against the real timeline.npz.

items.title: Fix flame visibility through smoke (teleop screenshot showed 2-pixel speck)
items.acceptance: Voxel-rendered flame is clearly visible behind dense smoke even with --compound-rgb=1; the second Beer-Lambert pass no longer erases the flame.
items.notes: Root causes: (a) flame_threshold=0.20 was higher than what trilinear interpolation yields at the flame envelope (0.05-0.30) so only the 0.6 source core survived as 1-2 pixels; (b) flame_emission_gain=4 was too low to penetrate dense smoke after attenuation; (c) compound_rgb=1 ran a second global Beer-Lambert that fogs flame pixels alongside everything else. Fix: lowered flame_threshold to 0.04 (and widened the smooth-step ramp to 0.05 above), bumped flame_emission_gain to 8.0, raised flame_smoke_passthrough default to 0.95, and added an optional flame_mask guard to _global_beer_lambert that blends the original voxel RGB back over flame pixels (with a Gaussian-dilated mask so the warm halo is preserved too). Quantified with a synthetic teleop-style scene (smoke wall in front of a 3x3x3 flame source): old defaults produced 0 warm pixels and max R-B=2; new defaults produce 24 warm pixels and max R-B=54; compound pass with the flame guard preserves all 24 pixels (without guard: 0).

items.title: Fix cross-numpy-version load failure in timeline.npz; restore staggered ignite times
items.acceptance: FireWorld.load works in conda env co-nav (numpy 1.24) regardless of which numpy wrote the npz; plan ignite_time_s values for the 4 new ignitions persisted.
items.notes: Root cause: propagation.py was saving meta as np.array([..], dtype=object) which forces pickle. The pickled string carried a numpy 2.x qualname (numpy._core), so loading under numpy 1.x raised ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'numpy._core'. Fix: write meta as a 0-d numpy unicode array under key 'meta_json' (no pickle), still emit the timeline_meta.json sidecar, and have FireWorld.load prefer the JSON sidecar -> meta_json -> legacy 'meta' (in that order) so old npzs keep loading too. Also: the kitchen/chair ignite_time_s values had reverted to 0; restored to 120/150/200/240. Reran propagation in /home/liushe10/miniconda3/envs/co-nav/bin/python so the cache is written by numpy 1.24 itself. Verified the new timeline reports first_flame at the expected timestamps for all 7 ignitions.

items.title: Author docs/fire_world_pipeline.md as the authoritative pipeline summary + paper-ready methodology
items.acceptance: docs/fire_world_pipeline.md walks through the 6 pipeline stages with implementation details and a self-contained methodology section that can be copied into a paper.
items.notes: Stage-by-stage write-up: (1) scene_scan with the sRGB OETF decode and per-face instance grouping, (2) planner templates + intensity presets + plan_id hashing, (3) reaction-diffusion-buoyancy-ceiling-jet voxel propagation, (4) FireScene runtime facade and the steps-per-unit / seconds-per-unit clock semantics, (5) FireSensorSuite voxel ray-march with dual-T flame channel + Beer-Lambert depth/radar/lidar/thermal, (6) integration into main.py / main_vec.py / keyboard_teleop_fire.py. Bottom half is a paper-ready methodology section with citations to Starr & Lattimer 2014 and a recommended ablation table. Appendix A is a file map; Appendix B is the minimal reproduction recipe.

items.title: Make voxel smoke actually fill the scene (was effectively invisible)
items.acceptance: After propagation, air-voxel smoke at eye height (1-1.7 m) reaches >5% coverage, persists through the full episode duration, and has plan smoke_yield as a controlling knob.
items.notes:
Diagnosed: smoke max=0.998 in the OLD timeline but mean=0.0003 (only ~100 voxels above 0.1 in 310k), all confined to ceiling 1.9-2.6m. Three root causes: (1) no smoke self-diffusion, so the plume was locked to the hot mask and pinned under the ceiling; (2) reaction-step smoke gain hard-coded at 0.5*burn_rate, divorced from the plan's smoke_yield; (3) sustained-source injection rate hard-coded at 0.10/s regardless of smoke_yield; plus a hidden mass leak: every transport substep cleared smoke in solid voxels, draining the room over ~30 s once the source stopped.

Fixes in utils/fire_world/propagation.py:
  * Added smoke self-diffusion (smoke_alpha=0.02 m^2/s) with CFL substep (smoke_cfl=0.08); solid-zero pulled OUT of the substep loop entirely so transport never leaks mass into walls.
  * smoke_buoy_frac=0.5 so smoke does not pin to the ceiling on the first step.
  * smoke_reaction_gain=4.0 (was 0.5) for reaction-driven production.
  * smoke_source_gain=4.0 multiplies the per-source rate by smoke_yield -> kitchen 0.85*4=3.4/s, bed 0.80*4=3.2/s. plan smoke_yield now actually drives room density.
  * smoke_decay_per_s=0.0008 (was 0.005) -> ~860 s half-life so a 900 s episode keeps a visible plume.
  * add_source(...) signature now carries smoke_yield through the source registry.
  * Removed solid-zero from the buoyancy and ceiling-jet steps - the renderer never samples through solids, so trapping smoke in walls is mass-conserved and harmless visually, but zeroing it caused the silent ~30 s leak.

New rule keys (all fall back to defaults so older plans still work):
  smoke_diffusivity, smoke_cfl, smoke_buoy_fraction, smoke_reaction_gain, smoke_source_gain, smoke_decay_per_s.

Verified: re-baked timeline.npz; air-voxel smoke at t=240s mean=0.078 (>200x the old 0.0003), 27% of air voxels above 0.05; plume persists to t=900s (68% air voxels >0.05). Eye-height layers (y=1.0-1.7 m) now have smoke max ~1.0 throughout 200-500 s.

items.title: Per-pixel depth/thermal in clean rooms; main.py and teleop dashboards consistent; flame spreads farther
items.acceptance: Depth in clean rooms is clean (mean err <0.05 m, 0% dropout); thermal pops on flame pixels (BGR diff >50); main.py uses thermal_color_blend=1.0 to match teleop; flame spread covers 2-3x more voxels per ignition.
items.notes:
Four problems fixed:

1. SmokeDepthSensor was driven by a single global smoke_density, so a clean room degraded identically to a smoky one. Refactored process() to accept a per-pixel transmittance from the voxel renderer; FireSensorSuite now passes voxel_out['transmittance'] in. local_density = clip(1 - T, 0, 1) drives noise sigma, dropout probability, and Jin's visibility cutoff per pixel. Verified: T=1.0 region has mean|err|=0.02 m & 0% dropout; T=0.1 region has 2.4 m err and 46% dropout.

2. Thermal panel hardly showed flame because compose_thermal didn't read flame_along (only temp_max), and the percentile auto-stretch let flame_c=600 dilute against scene luma. Added a 600 C floor on t_hi and an explicit flame_excess = clip(flame_along, 0, 1) * 600 contribution that drives flame pixels to the top of the colormap. Verified: flame patch BGR=(117,239,241) vs bg=(4,0,0) under INFERNO blend.

3. main.py and main_vec.py now construct VoxelSmokeConfig with thermal_color_blend=1.0, matching keyboard_teleop_fire's default, so the agent's thermal observation is the same colorized image users see in the teleop dashboard. (compound_rgb=0 is still the default, which together with T017's voxel-smoke fixes means main.py no longer needs the global Beer-Lambert pass to produce visible smoke.)

4. Flame spread was crawling: spread_speed=0.04 m/s + ignition_temp=350 C + spread mask requiring fuel>0 meant flame couldn't cross the air gap between disjoint pieces of furniture. Three changes in propagation.py / templates.py: spread_speed -> 0.18 m/s default; ignition_temp -> 200 C; new radiative_gain_c (250 C/s default, scaled by intensity) with a 4-cell box-blur kernel that pre-heats fuel within ~0.6 m of any flame voxel (NFPA 921 radiative pre-heating); spread_mask now is `(fuel>0) | (temp>t_ignite)` so flame can sustain itself while crossing pre-heated air. New rule keys (radiative_gain_c, radiative_radius_cells) added to plan.json for 83679a07b632 and the default rule generator. Verified on the existing plan: flame voxel count grows from 619 (t=0, source-only) to 1662 (t=240s); intense flame (>0.3) grows from 251 to 1015 voxels (4x).

items.title: Fire-time independent of robot steps: add wallclock mode + speedup
items.acceptance: main.py, main_vec.py and keyboard_teleop_fire.py all advance fire-time with real wall clock by default; --fire_speedup scales fire-seconds per real-second; legacy step mode still reachable via --fire_clock_mode=step.
items.notes:
Refactored FireClock to support two modes:
  * mode='wallclock' (default): uses time.monotonic() captured at clock.start(), returns base_t0_s + (now - origin) * speedup. Robot_step argument is ignored.
  * mode='step': legacy mapping t_sim = floor(N / steps_per_unit) * seconds_per_unit, used when reproducible benchmarks need bit-exact alignment to env.step() count.

FireScene.from_args reads new args (fire_clock_mode, fire_speedup) and calls clock.start() on construction. main.py and main_vec.py call fire_scene.clock.start() on every env.reset() so each episode starts at the same fire-time origin. keyboard_teleop_fire.py adds --clock-mode and --speedup flags, restarts the clock on R, and shows the active clock policy in the HUD overlay.

VoxelSmokeSensor.process and FireWorldController.render_for_agent now call scene.t_sim(robot_step) (the unified API) instead of the old scene.t_sim_for_step(robot_step), so wallclock mode is honored automatically; step mode still works because t_sim(robot_step) routes to t_sim_for_step internally when mode='step'.

Additional FireClock features used by future eval harnesses: pause()/resume() pair so an LLM-bound run can freeze fire-time while waiting for the API.

Verified: wallclock test (speedup=2 over 0.2s wall -> 0.4s fire-time, monotonic, ignores robot_step), pause/resume freezes t_sim within 0.02s, step-mode legacy test (50 steps -> 20.0s) passes. The existing scripts/test_fire_world_step_clock.py also still works against the real timeline.

items.title: Teleop: poll instead of block on cv2.waitKey so wallclock fire keeps evolving while the operator is idle
items.acceptance: When the user does not press any key, t_sim continues to increase in the HUD and flame/smoke continue evolving. Pressing 'p' toggles a freeze.
items.notes: Root cause: keyboard_teleop_fire.py used cv2.waitKey(0), which blocks the loop until a key is pressed. While blocked, the scene was never re-queried, so even though FireClock advanced internally the renderer never asked it for a fresh field. Fix: poll cv2.waitKey(POLL_MS=50) so the renderer re-queries the FireScene at ~20 FPS regardless of input. Frame dumps are now anchored to actual agent steps (not poll cycles) so we don't flood disk with idle frames. Added 'p' as a toggle that calls clock.pause()/resume(), useful when the operator wants to study a single frame without burning timeline. The HUD now shows 'PAUSED' when the wall clock is frozen.

items.title: Propagation: floors are semi-transparent thermal barriers; flame size scales with local fuel abundance; optional Gaussian spread kernel
items.acceptance: Multi-storey heat conducts across floors at attenuated rate (NFPA 921 §5.10); flame intensity in fuel-dense zones is visibly larger than in sparse zones; Gaussian spread kernel available as an alternative to the Laplacian.
items.notes:
Documented current model first: 6-step reaction-diffusion solver (heat Laplacian + smoke Laplacian + buoyancy + ceiling jet + reaction with k_burn=1/240 + Laplacian flame spread + decay/cooling/sustained sources) plus 2 enhancements (1-cell conduction and 4-cell radiative pre-heating). Reviewed your two requests:

1. 'Flame should not skip structural objects': true bug — the original code put walls + ceilings + floors all in a single zero-flux + force-to-ambient mask, which prevented vertical heat transfer across storeys. Fixed by treating floors separately as 'semi-transparent thermal barriers' (rule key floor_thermal_attenuation=0.20 default): the heat-diffusion Laplacian still runs through floors but the resulting Δtemp is multiplied by 0.20, so a fire on storey N raises the assembly temperature on storey N-1 over several minutes (matches NFPA 921 §5.10). Walls/ceilings remain zero-flux. flame_through_floors is a separate opt-in for letting flame voxels actually exist in floor decking; default 0 (heat path is enough to ignite fuel below).

2. 'Flame should grow when surrounded by fuel': the Laplacian transport is mass-conserving so total flame mass cannot grow from spread alone. The 'getting bigger' must come from the *reaction* term. Implemented fuel-abundance modulation: fuel_avg = box_blur_3d(fuel, k=2) gives a ~0.45 m neighbourhood mean; abundance = clip(fuel_avg/flammable_threshold, 0.5, 2.5) drives both burn_rate (multiplicative) AND flame_cap (0.85+0.15*abundance, clipped at 1.0). Sustained source pin bumped from 0.6*falloff to 0.95*falloff so the source itself can reflect the higher cap. Fixed a bug where np.clip(flame, 0, flame_cap) clipped DOWN existing flame values; replaced with 'grow only' clip (np.maximum(w.flame, np.minimum(grown, cap))).

3. Discussed Gaussian spread vs Laplacian: physically the Laplacian *is* an infinitesimal Gaussian step, so they're not fundamentally different transport models — both are mass-conserving smoothing operators. Gaussian gives larger isotropic radius per step + closer to NIST-FDS-validated plume shapes. Implemented as 3-iteration separable box-blur (sigma_cells = spread_speed*dt/v) controlled by rule key spread_kernel='laplacian'|'gaussian'. Plan 83679a07b632 now uses gaussian.

Also bumped sustain_s default from 0.5*duration to full remaining duration so plans without explicit sustain_s keep their sources alive through the whole episode.

Verified on plan 83679a07b632 after re-baking: flame max 0.95 (was 0.85), burning voxel count grows 619→1096 (1.77x) over 0→240s, intense flame (>0.3) grows 251→454 (1.81x), super-intense (>0.7) grows 7→25 (3.6x), maintains steady-state through 720s, smoke accumulates monotonically to mean=0.22 by end.

items.title: Inextinguishable point source + floor-as-fuel propagation + vertical flame column
items.acceptance: Single point source flame never goes out; fire spreads from the source across the floor to nearby furniture (room-filling); flames have a visible vertical extent rather than rendering as a flat blob.
items.notes:
User clarified the goal was NOT for air to burn but for fire to: (1) crawl across floors and ignite everything in a room, (2) never extinguish (so the user can keep watching), (3) display visible vertical flame height. Backed out the flashover air-burning logic from T021 and implemented three targeted features:

1. inextinguishable_sources=1 (default): the sustained-source step now ignores its sustain_s timer, and pins source fuel at 0.85*falloff each step. This guarantees the seven plan ignitions stay alive indefinitely.

2. Floor-as-fuel propagation. Step 4b deposits floor_fuel_value=0.7 of synthetic fuel into any floor voxel whose temperature crosses floor_ignite_temp_c=250 C. flame_through_floors defaults to 1 so the existing spread_mask + reaction loop can then burn the floor. Conduction & radiative gain were updated to also deposit heat into floor voxels (previously only fuel-bearing voxels). Result: kitchen fire crawls along the floor and ignites the dining chairs even without direct line-of-sight to the source.

3. Vertical flame column (step 8, post-source). For each non-zero flame voxel, project an upward plume of up to flame_column_cells=6 cells with geometric decay flame_column_decay=0.75/cell. Walls / ceilings clip the projection. A small fraction (0.05*dt*column) is added to smoke so the plume top contributes to the rising soot.

Also: radiative gain switched from box-MEAN to box-SUM (sqrt(window) normalised). Now each lit voxel acts as an independent point radiator, so densely-burning regions saturate nearby air quickly and the fire visibly expands outward in waves rather than asymptoting to a small static halo.

Verified on plan 83679a07b632 (rebaked): t=60s -> 744 voxels in 1.5x2.2m, t=120s -> 920 in 6.3x5.2m, t=240s -> 1255 in 6.3x6.0m (full room), holds through t=900s with fl_max=0.95 the whole time. Burning floor voxels grow 61 -> 420 (7x). Vertical column above the kitchen sink: peak flame=0.95 at y=0.86m, decays smoothly to flame=0.05 at y=2.5m (1.4 m visible column).

items.title: Fire actually spreads across the floor — two root causes (incorrect floor mask + spike-smoothing) fixed
items.acceptance: After ignition, fire spreads visibly across the floor and engulfs the room; burning floor voxels grow >90x; XZ coverage reaches the full storey footprint.
items.notes:
Two compounding bugs masked floor propagation:

1. scene_scan.rasterise_structural_voxels was stamping the full AABB of HM3D's ``floor`` and ``ceiling`` semantic instances. Those instances are single meshes whose AABB y-extent covers the entire storey height (e.g. 0..2.2 m), so the resulting voxel mask marked 20.5% of the world as 'floor' - effectively the entire room volume. Once the propagation step zero-fluxed those voxels back to ambient, no heat could survive long enough to ignite anything. Fixed by only stamping the bottom ``floor_slab_cells=2`` of a floor AABB (top ``ceiling_slab_cells=2`` for ceilings). The new floor mask is 2.4% of the world, occupying a clean 0.3 m slab at y=-0.04..0.11 m with realistic 19.9x10.3 m XZ footprint.

2. Step 4b's `(temp > floor_ignite_temp_c)` predicate was checked AFTER heat diffusion. The single-voxel thermal spike (a chair on fire at 900 C) was averaged out by the CFL-substepped Laplacian within one step (one substep absorbs 6*0.16 = 96% of the centre's excess into the 6 neighbours), so by the time floor ignition was evaluated the floor voxel just below the chair had cooled to ~60 C. Fix: add a 'direct contact' ignition path using a 3D box-SUM over flame voxels. Any floor voxel within ``floor_ignite_radius_cells=2`` of an active flame voxel (intensity > floor_flame_contact_thresh=0.2) gets the synthetic fuel deposit immediately, plus a seed flame intensity (0.3 * floor_fuel_value) and a forced temperature bump to (t_ignite + 50) so the next reaction step picks it up. The diffusion-based 'sustained heating' path is kept for the secondary effect (e.g. a fire on the storey above igniting the floor below).

Verified on plan 83679a07b632 (rebaked after re-scanning the scene):
  * t=0  -> burning=619,  floor=61,   XZ=1.5x1.5m
  * t=60  -> burning=938,  floor=159,  XZ=3.3x2.2m

items.title: Procedural flame texture: sub-voxel noise, time flicker, color jitter, smoke wisps; randomised floor ignition seed to break flat-sheet look
items.acceptance: Flame voxels show fractal texture rather than smooth blobs; flame visibly flickers with t_sim; floor flame has tongue-like heterogeneity instead of a uniform membrane.
items.notes:
Two-side fix:

1. Renderer side (utils/fire_sensors/voxel_render.py): added a 3-octave value-noise field cached per shape+seed, sampled trilinearly at each ray-march point with a time-domain y-offset so the texture 'scrolls upward'. Three modulations applied inside the per-step loop:
   * flame intensity = fl * (1 + flame_noise_strength*n + flame_edge_break*edge_weight*n), where edge_weight = 4*fl*(1-fl) peaks at fl=0.5. Result: ragged silhouette at the edge, stable bright core.
   * lut_input = clip(fl_used + flame_color_jitter*n_color, 0, 1) using a second seed. Result: same intensity samples flip between red/orange/yellow LUT bands, producing per-voxel color variation.
   * sm = sm * (1 + smoke_noise_strength*n_smoke). Result: plume has visible wisps instead of uniform grey.
   New params: flame_noise_strength=0.55, flame_edge_break=0.8, flame_color_jitter=0.25, flame_time_speed=12.0, smoke_noise_strength=0.30.
   t_sim plumbed through volumetric_composite -> VoxelSmokeSensor.process / FireWorldController.render_for_agent / runtime_process so wallclock advance drives flicker.

2. Propagation side (utils/fire_world/propagation.py): floor ignition now seeds each newly-ignited floor voxel with a uniform-random flame magnitude in [floor_seed_flame_min, floor_seed_flame_max] * floor_fuel_value (defaults 0.1-0.65). Temperature also jittered by 0..100 C extra. This breaks the 'flat membrane' look since adjacent floor voxels start with different intensities and propagation evolves them in lock-step but at different magnitudes.

Verified:
  * Floor flame std at t=240s = 0.07 across 3413 lit voxels (was uniform 0.21 before).
  * Flame pixel count in test render grew 64803 -> 97024 (heterogeneity makes more voxels visible at varying brightness).
  * Frame-to-frame flame-region delta ~4 RGB units = subtle but visible flicker.
  * Legacy step-clock test still passes; 5 files diagnostics clean.

All new params have plan.json overrides; defaults are tuned to give a 'lively but not noisy' fire. To disable any effect set the corresponding strength to 0.
